subject: Myth & Symbolism
title: Pythagoras and the Sacred Three
description: A short lesson to help you apply Pythagoras and the Sacred Three.

hook.text: Pythagoras called three the first real number. One is unity. Two is opposition. Three is harmony.

buildup.text: The Pythagoreans treated numbers as divine. Three was the number of completeness and cosmic balance.

discovery.text: A triangle is the simplest polygon. You need three points to define a plane. Geometry begins with three.

twist.text: Pythagoras didn't just study math—he ran a religious cult. Numbers were objects of worship, not just quantity.

climax.text: The idea that numbers are sacred started with Pythagoras. His cult made math and mysticism inseparable.

punchline.text: Math began as religion. Three was the proof.

quiz.question: What did Pythagoras believe about numbers?
